title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts Ledger Guide — Income Tax Withheld and the Waiver Income Count
content:
Income tax withheld from the benefits counted is excluded from the countable annual income on a Benefit Overpayment Accounts waiver request. The elections and deductions are read from the claimant's Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders and the deductions taken under them. The amount excluded is taken off the countable annual income.

| Elections on record | Tax excluded |
|---|---|
| An active Voluntary Federal Income Tax Withholding election | The federal tax withheld in the income window, multiplied by the annualizing multiplier of 4 |
| Only an active Voluntary State Income Tax Withholding election | The state tax withheld in the income window, multiplied by 4 |
| Neither election | Nothing |

## Dating the deductions

The deductions are dated the same way as the benefits counted: when a supplemental benefit payment was issued in the income window, each deduction is dated by the benefit week of the payment it was taken from; otherwise each is dated by the date it was taken. The income window is the three whole months before the handling date; a deduction falls in it when the whole months from its date to the handling date are fewer than 3.

## Reading the ledger

- Only elections with status active count.
- When both a federal and a state election are active, the federal row applies and the state tax withheld is not excluded.
- The federal tax withheld is the deduction entries taken under the federal election; the state tax withheld is those taken under the state election.

*Hypothetical:* an active federal election with USD 210.00 withheld in the window excludes USD 840.00. An active state election alone with USD 75.00 withheld in the window excludes USD 300.00.
